Mumbai, Oct 15 (PTI) Late arrival of sea breeze during the day and anti-cyclonic circulation over Gujarat and southwest Madhya Pradesh are among the factors that are leading to a rise in mercury levels in capital Mumbai and other parts of Maharashtra, meteorologists said on Thursday.
The Southwest Monsoon has withdrawn from the state and there are no signs of winter chill setting in. Temperatures across several parts of the state have been hovering around 35 degrees Celsius, an unusual phenomenon in the state for October.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow alert for heatwave for Mumbai for October 16.
“There is anti-cyclonic circulation over southwest Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. In this phenomenon, the wind subsides and there is warming. The surface is dry as there is no rainfall. Dry and hot wind is getting transferred from Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat,” Mahesh Palawat, Vice President of Meteorology at Skymet Weather Services, said.
The sea breeze is also getting delayed, especially in the case of Mumbai, he said.
“The sea breeze sets in around 12 noon, but it is now taking place at around 2-3 pm,” Palawat added.
According to him, some relief from the prevailing heat is expected next week.
“Sea breeze is likely to set in early and the effects of the anti-cyclone will come down,” Palawat added. PTI PR NP

Maharashtra weather update: Heatwave in Ratnagiri, rain forecast for Mumbai and Pune
While the bulletin forecasts a heatwave in isolated pockets of Ratnagiri, it does not explicitly indicate a yellow heat alert across Maharashtra. Several districts are expected to experience dry weather, while others may receive light to moderate rainfall accompanied by lightning and gusty winds
Ratnagiri is the only district specifically mentioned in the bulletin for a heatwave in isolated pockets on Thursday. File Pic
The India Meteorological Department (IMD), in its district-wise weather forecast issued on Thursday, has predicted hot and humid conditions in parts of the Konkan region, with a heatwave likely in isolated pockets of Ratnagiri on Thursday.
Rain, thundershowers and thunderstorms are also expected across several districts of Maharashtra over the next five days, from October 15 to October 19, 2026.
